claim: Mlekarna Planika dairy shop at Gregorčičeva 32 Kobarid stocks Tolminc PDO, local honey, sheep cheese, meat; shop open Mon-Fri (hours vary by season, e.g. Apr-May 7:00-19:00) with extended Jul-Aug Mon-Sat 7:00-20:00; closed Sundays.
quote: Apr 1 - May 31: Mon-Fri 7:00-19:00; Sat 7:00-14:00 ... Jul 1 - Aug 31: Mon-Sat 7:00-20:00 ... Sundays: Closed year-round

claim: The Cheese Museum (Od planine do Planike) at the Planika dairy offers guided tours Mon-Sat by advance booking, ~45 min (60 min with tasting), €6 adults / €4 children; tasting must be notified ≥3 working days ahead.
quote: Adults: €6.00 ... Children: €4.00 ... Groups can arrange visits Monday through Saturday by advance reservation. Tour duration is approximately 45 minutes, extending to one hour if a tasting is included.

claim: Mlekarna Planika is 100% farmer-owned and processes milk exclusively from 120-130 local farms across Tolmin, Kobarid, Bovec, Kanal, Nova Gorica, Cerkno and Idrija — making it the regional Tolminc PDO anchor producer.
quote: Today's Mlekarna Planika is the fourth largest dairy in Slovenia, and the only one that is 100% owned by farmers.

claim: Planika publishes a Sirarska pot (Cheese-Making Trail) brochure/map covering Posočje mountain dairies for self-guided exploration of Soča Valley alpine cheesemaking.
quote: PDF Brochure and a map of the Cheese Trail in the Soča Valley

claim: Beyond Planika, certified Tolminc PDO producers are the Tolminc Cheesemaking Association — Lovrč and Kumr farms in Čadrg (~15 km from Kobarid) and the Gugala dairy in Zatolmin near Tolmin gorges.
quote: the two certified producers are the Planika Dairy and the Tolminc Cheesemaking Association uniting three makers of PDO Tolminc cheese (the Lovrč and Kumr farms in Čadrg, and the Gugala dairy in Zatolmin)

claim: Tourist Farm Jelinčič in Soča (~25 km from Kobarid) produces traditional Bovški sir from ~110 indigenous Bovec ('trentarka') sheep and welcomes visitors for cheese, ricotta and curd-making demonstrations plus tastings; also offers rooms and a small camp.
quote: Boštjan now runs the farm and owns around 110 dairy sheep of the indigenous breed called Bovec sheep or 'trentarka' ... The owner will gladly show you how they produce cheese, curd and ricotta.

claim: Bovški sir has held PGI/PDO protected status since 2004; it is a dry-salted or brined sheep cheese aged ≥2 months giving an aromatic, slightly spicy character — a signature Bovec-area artisan product.
quote: Bovski cheese has been a protected geographical origin product since 2004 ... aged for a minimum of two months

claim: The 'Say Cheese' day experience (May-September, by prior appointment) packages two cheese-maker visits in Bovec + Kobarid Cheese Museum + frika lunch; 6-7 hours, €145/person (min 2).
quote: 2 cheese stops in the area of Bovec, Kobarid, and Tolmin ... 6-7 hours, accommodates 1-4 participants, and costs 145 EUR per person (minimum 2 people)

claim: Hiša Polonka, Hiša Franko's sister bistro at Gregorčičeva 1 in central Kobarid, serves Soča Valley classics (frika, žlikrofi, Kobariški štruklji, game) plus FEO craft beer brewed by Valter Kramar; open Mon/Thu/Fri 17:00-22:00 and Sat-Sun 12:00-15:00 / 18:00-22:00.
quote: Monday, Thursday, Friday: 17:00-22:00 ... Saturday, Sunday: 12:00-15:00 / 18:00-22:00 ... pivovarna Feo, imenovana po Ivanu Volariču

claim: Restaurant Kotlar (Trg svobode 11, central Kobarid) serves Adriatic/Mediterranean cuisine — grilled fish €15.50-23, risotto/pasta €12.50-14.80, daily fresh fish €50-62/kg; open Mon-Thu 12:00-22:00, Fri-Sun 12:00-23:00; reservations recommended.
quote: Monday–Thursday: 12:00–22:00 ... Friday–Sunday: 12:00–23:00 ... Fish dishes (grilled dorada, sea bass, trout fillets) ranging €15.50–€23.00

claim: Topli Val (Hotel Hvala, Kobarid) is the 45-year-old Hvala-family Mediterranean/seafood restaurant featuring oysters, trout, fish carpaccio and the traditional Kobariški štruklji dessert; reservations required.
quote: Topli Val has been serving impeccable seafood from the Slovenian Adriatic for around 45 years ... you should not leave without trying the traditional dessert »Kobariški štruklji«

claim: Jestival – Food & Art Festival fills central Kobarid 11:00-21:00 on the first Saturday of October, showcasing local Soča Valley restaurants, mountain-pasture cheese, Kobariški štruklji, honey and salami producers — the key annual food day-trip target.
quote: On the first Saturday of October, the centre of Kobarid will be filled with the smell of local culinary delights from the Soča valley ... 11am to 9pm at the Kobarid main square

claim: Thirsty River Brewing in Bovec (~30 km from Kobarid) is a craft microbrewery and taproom on Bovec main square brewing 400 L ale batches and a distilling line (gin, young whiskey, vodka, coffee liqueur); brewery tours by prior arrangement.
quote: small, 400 liter batches of all styles of ales ... line of Thirsty River Liquor including a delicious Gin, Young Whiskey as well as Vodka and coffee liqueur ... Tours of the brewery are available by prior arrangement

claim: Goriška Brda's wine capital Dobrovo is ~48 km / 45-minute drive from Kobarid, placing Brda wineries (Movia, Simčič, Klinec, Klet Brda) clearly OUT of a 30-km radius — wine day-trips are feasible but not 'near'.
quote: The driving distance between Kobarid to Dobrovo is 30 miles (approximately 48 kilometers), and it takes approximately 45 minutes to drive from Kobarid to Dobrovo

claim: Kobarid offers apitherapy and honey-massage experiences with overnight stays 'in the company of bees' — a beekeeper-visit option directly in town.
quote: In the Soča Valley, in Kobarid, you can enjoy apitherapy and honey massages in a beehive, and you can also stay overnight in the company of bees

claim: Aqua Tours Bovec runs a sheep-breeding and cheese-making excursion meeting a local Bovški-sir cheesemaker, touring the cellar and tasting whey, curd, yoghurt and aged sheep cheese — a turnkey artisan-producer day-trip from Kobarid.
quote: meet a local cheese-maker who produces a delicious sheep cheese, slightly spicy with full taste. Observe a master cheesemaker at work and walk into the cheese maker's heaven (his cheese cellar)
